{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Chalmers W. Sherwin''' (1916–1998) was an American [[physicist]].

He was born at Two Harbors, Minnesota and gained a B.S. degree at [[Wheaton College (Illinois)]] and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1940. He worked in the Radiation Laboratory of [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] from 1941 to 1945, where as part of the war effort he helped in the development of an advanced distant-warning system and airplane-mounted radar. He then worked as an assistant in the physics department at [[Columbia University]] in 1946 before becoming assistant professor of physics at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois]] and professor of physics there in 1951. From 1954 to 1955 he was on secondment to the [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] as [[Chief Scientist of the U.S. Air Force]]. <ref> {{cite book|title=Government and Science: Review of the National Science ..., Volume 1; Volume 4|page=815}} </ref>

From 1961 he worked at [[The Aerospace Corporation|Aerospace Corporation]]. As head of research at [[General Atomics|General Atomic]], he oversaw the development of a [[Artificial heart valve|carbon heart valve]].  He wrote two college physics texts and secured numerous patents.<ref name=ucal>{{cite web|title=Welcome to the University of Chicago Magazine Online|date=2007-05-15|accessdate=2016-04-19|url=https://magazine.uchicago.edu/9808/html/deaths.html}}</ref> Around 1959 as a physicist at the University of Illinois, he had suggested a computerised learning system which would eventually become the [[PLATO (computer system)|PLATO]] system in 1960.<ref>{{cite web|title=PLATO: From Computer-Based Education to Corporate Social Responsibility
|date=2003-11-05|accessdate=2016-04-19|url=http://www.cbi.umn.edu/iterations/vanmeer.html#III |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315104854/http://www.cbi.umn.edu/iterations/vanmeer.html#III |archive-date=15 March 2018 }}</ref>

He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1946. <ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=S&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|accessdate= 7 June 2020}} </ref> He died on February 20, 1998<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Phipps Jr. |first=Thomas |date=October 1998 |title=In Memory: Chalmers W. Sherwin |url=https://www.naturalphilosophy.org/pdf/abstracts/abstracts_1276.pdf |journal=Apeiron |volume=5 |issue=3-4 |pages=234-235}}</ref>
